name: Karavasta Lagoon (Divjaka-Karavasta National Park)
blurb: Adriatic lagoon where Dalmatian pelicans, flamingos and egrets fish the shallows.

tip.title: Remove the mullet
tip.text: Fish like mullet feed the pelican, egret and cormorant. Set Flathead grey mullet to -100% and watch which fish-eating birds and predators lose food.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm Mediterranean sunshine drives growth of the lagoon algae, reeds, salt-marsh plants and pines.

nodes.name: Brackish lagoon water
nodes.desc: A shallow, low-salinity lagoon cut off from the Adriatic by a sand strip, rich in algae and dense aquatic plants.

nodes.name: River sediment and nutrients
nodes.desc: The lagoon was formed from sediment carried down by the Shkumbin and Seman rivers, which also feed it with nutrients.

nodes.name: Coastal sand dunes
nodes.desc: A sandy barrier separates the lagoon from the sea; salt-tolerant plants and later pines settle and stabilise it.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead reeds, algae, pine litter and animal remains, returning nutrients to the mud and water.

nodes.name: Lagoon algae
nodes.desc: Microscopic and mat-forming algae in the nutrient-rich shallows form the base of the aquatic food chain.

nodes.name: Glasswort
nodes.desc: A salt-tolerant succulent of salt marshes and lagoon margins, among the well-recorded plants around the lagoon.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: Forms dense reed beds along wetland edges, giving shelter and nesting cover for birds and amphibians.

nodes.name: Aleppo pine
nodes.desc: A Mediterranean pine of the sandy coastal forests, which are increasingly dominated by pines.

nodes.name: Mastic tree
nodes.desc: An evergreen Mediterranean shrub of coastal scrub, whose berries are eaten by some mammals.

nodes.name: Northern house mosquito
nodes.desc: Larvae develop in standing water and feed on algae and organic particles; adults are prey for frogs and other animals.

nodes.name: Flathead grey mullet
nodes.desc: Tolerates fresh, brackish and salt water and often enters lagoons, grazing on algae and detritus.

nodes.name: Greater flamingo
nodes.desc: Filters mud and water for small crustaceans, algae, insect larvae and molluscs; its eggs and chicks are taken by gulls.

nodes.name: European badger
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats fruits such as mastic berries along with amphibians and other small animals.

nodes.name: Little egret
nodes.desc: The most recorded bird around the lagoon; it stalks shallows for fish, amphibians and insects.

nodes.name: Pygmy cormorant
nodes.desc: A small cormorant that hunts fish, often in groups, in vegetated pools and lagoons.

nodes.name: Marsh frog
nodes.desc: A large water frog of ponds and wetlands that eats insects and other small prey.

nodes.name: Dice snake
nodes.desc: A semi-aquatic snake that hunts fish and amphibians in water.

nodes.name: Yellow-legged gull
nodes.desc: A widespread coastal gull that eats fish and other food, and raids flamingo eggs and chicks.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: An adaptable predator of frogs, snakes and wetland birds around the lagoon margins.

nodes.name: Dalmatian pelican
nodes.desc: Holds about 5% of the world population and is the only coastal breeding site on the Adriatic and Ionian seas; it eats fish such as mullet.

nodes.name: Golden jackal
nodes.desc: An opportunistic predator and scavenger of rodents, birds, frogs and snakes, and a threat to pelican eggs.
